A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Wolfpack/WALL research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original SMAC experiments comparing attacks and robust MARL policies, with additional algorithm comparisons, ablations, and case studies in Appendices E–G.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical evaluations and adds MPE experiments, measured training times, and robustness results under observation noise and reduced allied-unit health.

M1.justification: The initial attack, KL-based follow-up selection, Transformer-based attack timing, and WALL training procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and the implementation objectives in Appendix B are retained; applying the method to MPE does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates six SMAC scenarios. v3 retains these and adds three MPE predator-prey scenarios: PP 3/1, PP 6/2, and PP 9/3. Appendix E.5 also adds distinct SMAC test conditions involving Gaussian observation noise and reduced allied-unit health.

E2.justification: The original SMAC comparisons retain their attack and defense comparators, including EGA, RANDOM, RARL, RAP, ERNIE, and ROMANCE. The added MPE and perturbation experiments reuse Vanilla QMIX, RANDOM, and ROMANCE; no new comparison method is introduced or removed from a retained experiment.

E3.justification: New MPE evaluations report cumulative rewards over the last 100 episodes and specify four attack steps, one Wolfpack attack, and follow-up group sizes of 1, 3, and 5. Appendix E.5 introduces standard Gaussian observation noise at 8/16 randomly selected attack steps and allied-health reductions of 10%, 15%, and 20%. Existing SMAC training budgets and hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix E.4 compares computational costs, while E.5 tests whether robustness learned against action attacks transfers to observation noise and environment-parameter shifts. These substantially extend the analysis beyond the retained component ablations, hyperparameter sweeps, and agent-selection case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five random seeds and report means with standard deviations in tables and shaded curves. Additional performance results follow this practice. Revised standard-deviation values change reported results, without documenting a different uncertainty-estimation procedure or increased run count.

E6.justification: v3 adds MPE rewards, training times, and perturbation win rates; for example, Table E.4 reports Gaussian-noise mean win rates of 94.3% for WALL and 73.1% for ROMANCE. Retained results also change: RAP's Random Attack mean changes from 86 to 83.0 in the main SMAC table, despite unchanged scenario means. Table E.1 changes VDN-based RAP's 3m Natural standard deviation from 48.4 to 1.8. Most existing means and learning-curve findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds a formal collision-based reward definition for the new MPE tasks. The existing Dec-POMDP and Wolfpack definitions, convergence argument attributed to prior work, selection equations, and appendix objectives remain unchanged; no new proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: coordinated Wolfpack attacks disrupt cooperation, follow-up selection and critical-step planning strengthen attacks, and WALL improves robustness. The added experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new perturbation results as broader distribution-shift robustness and argues that the additional training cost is justified. Its revised limitations drop v1's recurrent-network substitution suggestion and assert that extended baseline training cannot close the gap, although no corresponding extended-training comparison is reported. Section 4.5 also broadens the stated applicability to most CTDE algorithms.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a WALL code-access link, MPE environment specifications and attack hyperparameters in Appendices A.1/C.3, and measured training times in E.4. Core implementation, hardware, and SMAC hyperparameters remain substantially unchanged; some detailed SMAC feature-dimension formulas are condensed into prose.

R1.justification: v3 adds Lowe et al. (2017) and Terry et al. (2021) for MPE and PettingZoo, and adjusts some attack-citation categorization in related work. The overall positioning against existing robust MARL and adversarial-attack approaches is retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative remain intact. Changes include rewriting the SMAC observation/state description, organizing Appendix A by environment, adding acknowledgments and appendix navigation, and moving revised limitations from Appendix H into main-text Section 6.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the displays with MPE results and environment illustrations, a new environment-specification table, and computational-cost and perturbation-result tables. Table C.3 gains MPE configurations, existing SMAC table headers are simplified, and several appendix figures are repositioned. Existing learning curves and case-study imagery are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence that was previously confined to SMAC action attacks: MPE provides a second domain, and Appendix E.5 directly tests robustness to observation and environment shifts. Measured training costs and a code-access link also improve practical assessability. These gains outweigh localized reporting problems, particularly the inconsistent RAP mean in Table 2 and the unsupported extended-training assertion in the revised limitations.
